newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia bid to settle rubber row with Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia bid to settle rubber row with Malaysia.

text.p: Indonesia has proposed talks with Malaysia to end a row over which country should provide the next executive director of the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO), Antara news agency reported on Wednesday.
The official Indonesian news agency quoted Agricultural Minister Sjarifudin Baharsjah as saying that the two sides should hold talks to solve the problem.
However, Sjarifudin maintained that Indonesia had the right to nominate a candidate to the top post in the INRO.
Malaysia said it was its turn to hold the executive director's post under an unofficial rotation scheme, but Indonesia argues that Malaysia already has the privilege of hosting the INRO secretariat.
Earlier this week Malaysia said that it was unlikely to sign a new global rubber pact if Indonesia refused to withdraw its bid.
The Third International Natural Rubber Agreement (INRA III) was agreed in Geneva last year but both Malaysia and Indonesia must still sign the pact.
Indonesia held the post of executive director under the term of the First International Rubber Agreement (INRA I).
INRO is made up of 23 major natural rubber consuming countries and six major producing nations.
Antara did not give further details.
